subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger child what a fire needs to burn, why a fire goes out when it is covered, and why children must never play with fire.
prompt_hi: Ek chhote bachche ko samjhao ki aag ko jalne ke liye kya chahiye, dhakne pe aag kyon bujh jaati hai, aur bachchon ko aag se kabhi kyon nahi khelna chahiye.
answer: A fire needs fuel, oxygen from the air and enough heat; covering it cuts off the oxygen so it goes out. Fire spreads fast and burns skin, so only adults should handle it.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: is burning a physical or a chemical change, and what does it give out?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: jalna physical badlav hai ya chemical, aur isse kya nikalta hai?
answer: A chemical change; it gives out heat and light, and makes new substances such as carbon dioxide.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name three things that can carry away broken rock and soil.
prompt_hi: 3 cheezein batao jo tooti chattan aur mitti ko bahaa ke le ja sakti hain.
answer: Any three of: flowing water (rivers and rain), wind, moving ice (glaciers), sea waves.

subject: science
prompt_en: Put a few small pieces of chalk, or a few sugar cubes, into a closed steel tiffin box or plastic bottle and shake it hard for three minutes. Predict what the pieces will look like and what you will find at the bottom.
prompt_hi: Chalk ke kuch chhote tukde, ya kuch sugar cubes, ek band steel ke tiffin ya plastic ki bottle mein daalo aur 3 minute zor se hilaao. Guess karo tukde kaise dikhenge aur neeche kya milega.
answer: Their corners become rounded and they get smaller, and fine powder collects at the bottom, just as rocks become rounded pebbles and sand in a stream.

subject: science
prompt_en: Outdoors, make two small slopes of soil in trays: one bare, one covered with grass or a layer of leaves. Pour one mug of water slowly on each from the same height. Predict which slope loses more soil.
prompt_hi: Bahar do tray mein mitti ki do chhoti dhalaan banao: ek khaali, ek ghaas ya patton ki parat se dhaki. Har ek pe ek hi oonchai se dheere dheere ek mug paani daalo. Guess karo kaunsi dhalaan se zyada mitti bahegi.
answer: The bare slope loses more soil; the grass or leaves hold the soil and slow the water down.

subject: science
prompt_en: Fill a small plastic bottle completely with water, close it tightly, put it in a plastic bag and leave it in the freezer overnight. Predict what will happen to the bottle, and how this explains cracks in rocks on cold mountains.
prompt_hi: Ek chhoti plastic ki bottle ko poora paani se bharo, kas ke band karo, plastic ki thaili mein rakho aur raat bhar freezer mein chhod do. Guess karo bottle ka kya hoga, aur isse thande pahadon ki chattanon mein daraar kaise samajh aati hai.
answer: The bottle bulges or even splits, because water expands when it freezes. In rocks, water in cracks freezes and expands, pushing the cracks wider until pieces break off.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why are the pebbles in a mountain stream round and smooth, while rocks freshly broken from a cliff are sharp?
prompt_hi: Pahaadi nadi ke kankar gol aur chikne kyon hote hain, jabki chattan se abhi toote tukde nukile hote hain?
answer: As the stream carries the pebbles, they knock and rub against each other and the riverbed for a long time, wearing away their sharp edges; fresh pieces have not been rubbed yet.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare: (A) in Rajasthan, hot days and cold nights make rock surfaces crack and peel; (B) wind blows sand across the Thar desert and piles it into dunes. Which is weathering and which is erosion?
prompt_hi: Tulna karo: (A) Rajasthan mein garam din aur thandi raatein chattanon ki sataha mein daraar daal ke chhilka utaar deti hain; (B) hawa Thar registaan mein ret uda ke tibbe bana deti hai. Kaunsa weathering hai aur kaunsa erosion?
answer: A is weathering (rock breaking where it is); B is erosion, with the wind carrying sand and dropping it in dunes.

subject: science
prompt_en: A peepal tree is growing out of a crack in an old wall. What will happen to the wall over many years, and what is this an example of?
prompt_hi: Ek purani deewar ki daraar se peepal ka ped ug raha hai. Kai saalon mein deewar ka kya hoga, aur ye kiska example hai?
answer: The roots grow thicker and push the crack wider until the wall breaks apart; this is weathering by plants.

subject: science
prompt_en: After forests on a hill are cut down, villages below see muddier rivers and more landslides. Explain this using erosion.
prompt_hi: Pahadi ke jungle kaatne ke baad neeche ke gaon mein nadiyaan zyada matmaili ho jaati hain aur zyada landslide hote hain. Erosion se ise samjhao.
answer: Tree roots hold the soil together and leaves slow the rain; without trees, rain erodes the soil quickly, rivers carry the mud downhill, and loosened slopes slide.

subject: science
prompt_en: Tushar says, 'Soil is easy to replace; if rain washes it away, new soil will form by next year.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Tushar kehta hai, 'Mitti ko badalna aasaan hai; agar baarish use bahaa le jaaye, toh agle saal tak nayi mitti ban jaayegi.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Soil forms very slowly from weathered rock and humus; a few centimetres can take hundreds of years, so lost soil cannot be replaced in a year.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a river's journey from the mountains to the sea in three parts. Label where you would find big sharp rocks, rounded pebbles, and fine sand and mud. Explain the pattern.
prompt_hi: Pahadon se samudra tak nadi ka safar 3 hisson mein banao. Label karo ki bade nukile patthar, gol kankar, aur baarik ret aur keechad kahaan milenge. Pattern samjhao.
answer: Mountains: big sharp rocks, freshly broken. Middle: rounded pebbles, rubbed while being carried. Near the sea, on the plains and in the delta: fine sand and mud, dropped where the river slows (for example the Sundarbans delta).

subject: science
prompt_en: Using the chalk-in-a-box experiment, explain to a friend how a mountain stream turns rocks into pebbles and sand.
prompt_hi: Chalk-in-a-box experiment ki madad se apne dost ko samjhao ki pahaadi nadi chattanon ko kankar aur ret mein kaise badal deti hai.
answer: Like the shaken chalk, rocks carried by a stream knock and rub against each other and the riverbed; over a long time their edges wear off, they get rounder and smaller, and finally break into sand.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: name one thing that can break rocks without any people being involved.
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: ek aisi cheez batao jo bina kisi insaan ke chattanon ko tod sakti hai.
answer: Any one of: water freezing in cracks, plant roots, heating and cooling, rainwater.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name three physical changes that happen during adolescence.
prompt_hi: Adolescence ke dauraan hone wale 3 shaaririk badlav batao.
answer: Any three of: a growth spurt in height, the voice getting deeper, new hair growth (for example in the underarms), more sweat and oil (body odour, pimples), changes in body shape, and periods starting in girls.

subject: science
prompt_en: On screen is a height chart of five friends from age 9 to 16, with the later years hidden. Before you see them, predict: will all five have their biggest growth jump in the same year?
prompt_hi: Screen pe paanch doston ka 9 se 16 saal tak ka height chart hai, aage ke saal chhupe hue hain. Dekhne se pehle guess karo: kya paanchon ki sabse badi lambai ki chhalaang ek hi saal mein hogi?
answer: No. Each friend has a growth spurt at a different age; girls often have it a little earlier than boys. Different timing is normal.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your height mark on the wall was 135 cm at age 10 and 137 cm at 11. Predict: will you keep growing only 2 cm a year until you are 18?
prompt_hi: Deewar pe tumhari lambai ka nishaan 10 saal pe 135 cm aur 11 saal pe 137 cm tha. Guess karo: kya tum 18 saal tak har saal sirf 2 cm hi badhoge?
answer: Probably not. During the adolescent growth spurt many people grow much faster, sometimes several centimetres in a year; afterwards growth slows and usually stops by the late teens.

subject: science
prompt_en: What causes the body to change during adolescence?
prompt_hi: Adolescence ke dauraan shareer mein badlav kis wajah se hote hain?
answer: Hormones: chemical messengers released into the blood that signal the body to grow and mature.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why do many adolescents notice more sweat and body odour, and what helps?
prompt_hi: Bahut se adolescents ko zyada paseena aur shareer ki gandh kyon mehsoos hoti hai, aur isme kya madad karta hai?
answer: Sweat glands become more active; bacteria on the skin act on sweat and cause the smell. A daily bath, washing the underarms, and clean clothes and socks help.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare how the voice changes in boys and in girls during adolescence.
prompt_hi: Adolescence mein ladkon aur ladkiyon ki aawaaz kaise badalti hai, tulna karo.
answer: Both voices get deeper. In boys the voice box grows more, so the voice becomes much deeper, may crack for a while, and an Adam's apple may show; in girls the change is smaller and less noticeable.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two cousins, Priya and Arjun, are both 12. At a family wedding, Priya is taller than Arjun this year, though last year Arjun was taller. Is this normal? Why?
prompt_hi: Do cousins, Priya aur Arjun, dono 12 saal ke hain. Ek shaadi mein Priya is saal Arjun se lambi hai, jabki pichhle saal Arjun lamba tha. Kya ye normal hai? Kyon?
answer: Yes. Girls often begin their growth spurt earlier than boys, so they can be taller for a while; boys often catch up and grow later.

subject: science
prompt_en: A sports coach picks 12-year-olds for a team only by their height. Using what you know about adolescence, why might this be unfair?
prompt_hi: Ek sports coach 12 saal ke bachchon ko sirf unki lambai dekh ke team mein chunta hai. Adolescence ke baare mein jo jaante ho, uske hisaab se ye unfair kyon ho sakta hai?
answer: Children grow at different ages; a child who is short at 12 may grow a lot later. Height at 12 does not show final height or ability, so skill should be judged instead.

subject: science
prompt_en: Mohit says, 'Pimples come only from eating samosas, so if I stop eating them I'll never get pimples.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Mohit kehta hai, 'Pimples sirf samose khaane se hote hain, toh agar main samose band kar doon toh kabhi pimples nahi honge.' Kya galat hai?
answer: Pimples in adolescence happen mainly because hormones make the skin's oil glands more active and pores get blocked. Gentle face washing and a balanced diet can help, but no single food is the only cause.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a simple timeline from age 8 to 20. Mark roughly when the growth spurt often happens for many girls and for many boys, and when growth usually stops.
prompt_hi: 8 se 20 saal tak ki ek simple timeline banao. Lagbhag mark karo ki kai ladkiyon aur kai ladkon ki growth spurt aksar kab hoti hai, aur lambai badhna aam taur pe kab rukta hai.
answer: Many girls: roughly 10 to 13; many boys: roughly 12 to 15; growth usually stops in the late teens. These are rough ranges, and each person is different.

subject: science
prompt_en: Your younger cousin is worried because her friends have started growing faster than her. Explain to her why this is normal.
prompt_hi: Tumhari chhoti cousin pareshaan hai kyonki uske dost usse jaldi lambe hone lage hain. Use samjhao ki ye normal kyon hai.
answer: Everyone's body changes when its own hormones start the changes, which can be at different ages over several years; starting later is normal, and her growth spurt will come. She can ask a parent or doctor anything she wants to know.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what are the chemical messengers that bring about the changes of adolescence called?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: adolescence ke badlav laane wale chemical messengers ko kya kehte hain?
answer: Hormones.

subject: science
prompt_en: Name three trusted people a student could talk to about worries while growing up.
prompt_hi: 3 aise bharosemand logon ke naam batao jinse ek student badhte waqt apni chintaon ke baare mein baat kar sakta hai.
answer: For example: a parent, a class teacher, a school counsellor, a doctor, an elder sibling or another trusted adult in the family.

subject: science
prompt_en: A class puts up an anonymous question box about growing up. Predict: will most questions be very different from each other, or will many students ask similar things? What does that tell you?
prompt_hi: Ek class mein badhne ke baare mein bina naam ka question box rakha gaya. Guess karo: zyadatar sawaal ek doosre se bilkul alag honge, ya bahut se students milte-julte sawaal poochhenge? Isse kya pata chalta hai?
answer: Many students will ask similar questions. Most people share the same worries, so nobody is alone and asking is normal.

subject: science
prompt_en: Predict: if someone keeps a worry completely to themselves for weeks, will it usually feel bigger or smaller over time? And what usually happens after they share it with a trusted adult?
prompt_hi: Guess karo: agar koi apni chinta hafton tak bilkul apne tak rakhe, toh samay ke saath wo aksar badi lagegi ya chhoti? Aur bharosemand bade se share karne ke baad aksar kya hota hai?
answer: Kept inside, a worry often feels bigger; after sharing it with a trusted adult it usually feels lighter, and together they can find a way to deal with it.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is it normal to have strong or changing feelings during adolescence?
prompt_hi: Adolescence ke dauraan tez ya badalti bhaavnaayein hona normal kyon hai?
answer: Hormones and many big changes in the body, school and friendships all happen at once, and the brain is still developing; everyone goes through this.

subject: science
prompt_en: Why is it better to check information about growing up with a trusted adult, a doctor or a textbook rather than only with a friend or a random online video?
prompt_hi: Badhne ke baare mein jaankari kisi dost ya random online video ki bajaye bharosemand bade, doctor ya textbook se check karna kyon behtar hai?
answer: Friends and random videos can spread myths and wrong information; trusted adults, doctors and textbooks give correct and safe information.

subject: science
prompt_en: Compare two ways Kabir handles stress before exams: (A) staying up all night on his phone and skipping meals; (B) sleeping on time, playing for half an hour and talking to his elder sister. Which helps more, and why?
prompt_hi: Exam se pehle tension sambhaalne ke Kabir ke do tareekon ki tulna karo: (A) poori raat phone pe jaagna aur khaana chhodna; (B) time pe sona, aadha ghanta khelna aur badi behen se baat karna. Kaunsa zyada madad karta hai, aur kyon?
answer: B, because sleep, physical activity and talking reduce stress and help the brain focus and remember; A makes tiredness, mood and concentration worse.

subject: science
prompt_en: Some friends dare Ishaan to try tobacco 'just once'. What is a healthy way for him to respond?
prompt_hi: Kuch dost Ishaan ko 'bas ek baar' tobacco try karne ki challenge dete hain. Uske liye accha jawaab kya hoga?
answer: Say no firmly, walk away or suggest doing something else, and tell a trusted adult if the pressure continues. Tobacco is harmful and addictive, and real friends respect a no.

subject: science
prompt_en: A friend tells you they have felt very sad for weeks and don't want to do anything. What could you do to help?
prompt_hi: Ek dost tumhe batata hai ki wo hafton se bahut udaas hai aur kuch karne ka mann nahi karta. Uski madad ke liye tum kya kar sakte ho?
answer: Listen kindly without making fun, encourage them to tell a trusted adult such as a parent, teacher or counsellor, and offer to go with them; if they seem unsafe, tell an adult straight away. Tele-MANAS (14416) and Childline (1098) are free helplines.

subject: science
prompt_en: Neel says, 'Talking about body changes is shameful; grown-up people never ask questions.' What is wrong?
prompt_hi: Neel kehta hai, 'Body changes ke baare mein baat karna sharm ki baat hai; samajhdaar log sawaal nahi poochhte.' Kya galat hai?
answer: These changes are natural and happen to everyone; asking trusted adults or doctors is a sensible, grown-up thing to do, and it prevents myths and worry.

subject: science
prompt_en: Draw a 'circle of trust' with yourself in the centre and at least four trusted people or places around you. Next to each, write one thing you could talk to them about.
prompt_hi: Ek 'circle of trust' banao jismein beech mein tum ho aur charon taraf kam se kam chaar bharosemand log ya jagah. Har ek ke paas likho ki unse kis baare mein baat kar sakte ho.
answer: For example: parent (body changes, worries); class teacher or school counsellor (school stress, bullying); doctor (health questions); elder sibling or cousin (friendships); Childline 1098 (if ever unsafe).

subject: science
prompt_en: Explain to a younger cousin who is about to start Class 7 what kinds of feelings might change and who they can talk to.
prompt_hi: Apne chhote cousin ko, jo Class 7 shuru karne wala hai, samjhao ki kaunsi bhaavnaayein badal sakti hain aur wo kisse baat kar sakta hai.
answer: Moods can change quickly, you may want more independence and care more about looks and friends; this is normal. Talk to parents, teachers, a counsellor or a doctor, and use sleep, play and hobbies to feel better.

subject: science
prompt_en: From last time: what number can a child in India call for free if they are in trouble or unsafe?
prompt_hi: Pichhli baar se: Bharat mein agar koi bachcha musibat mein ho ya surakshit na ho, toh wo kaunsa number free mein call kar sakta hai?
answer: Childline 1098 (and Tele-MANAS 14416 for emotional and mental health support).

subject: science
prompt_en: Name three iron-rich foods that are common in Indian homes.
prompt_hi: 3 aise iron se bharpoor khaane batao jo Indian gharon mein aam hain.
answer: For example: spinach (palak), methi and other green leafy vegetables, jaggery (gur), chana, rajma, dates, bajra, and eggs for those who eat them.

subject: science
prompt_en: Two lunches have the same palak dal. One is eaten with a glass of lemon water, the other with a cup of tea. Predict which helps the body take in more iron.
prompt_hi: Do lunch mein ek jaisi palak dal hai. Ek ke saath nimbu-paani piya jaata hai, doosre ke saath ek cup chai. Guess karo kaunsa shareer ko zyada iron lene mein madad karega.
answer: The one with lemon water: vitamin C helps the body absorb iron, while substances in tea reduce iron absorption.
